skill.name: apify-actor-development
skill.description: Develop, debug, test, document, and deploy Apify Actors for web scraping, automation, data processing, and Standby HTTP services.
skill.summary: Build production-ready Apify Actors with guided setup, schemas, testing, deployment, security, and marketplace documentation.
skill.author: apify

security_audit.summary: Most detections are false positives from Markdown code spans, safe project paths, examples, and defensive warnings. Two static findings remain confirmed: command-line secret exposure and unpinned execution of `@playwright/mcp@latest`. Semantic review also found query-string token guidance and mandatory tool and model attribution.

remediation.issue: Standby authentication permits API tokens in URL query parameters.
remediation.suggestion: Require the Authorization header and remove query-token examples. Explain that URLs can persist in logs, history, monitoring, and referrer data.

remediation.issue: The secrets command places a secret value in a command argument.
remediation.suggestion: Use a CLI-supported secure prompt or input channel. Never place secret values in process arguments or reusable shell history.

remediation.issue: The Playwright MCP command uses the mutable `latest` package tag.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed package version and document how maintainers verify and update that version.

remediation.issue: Tool and model attribution is mandatory in deployable metadata.
remediation.suggestion: Make attribution optional and obtain user approval before adding metadata intended for monitoring.

content.value_statement: Building production-ready Actors requires coordinated code, schemas, tests, deployment settings, and documentation. This skill guides that workflow for scraping, automation, and HTTP services.
actual_capabilities: Scaffolds Apify Actor projects in JavaScript, TypeScript, or Python.
Guides input, output, dataset, key-value store, and Actor configuration schemas.
Supports local testing with Apify CLI, logs, and local storage inspection.
Guides Actor discovery, remote calls, deployment, and platform execution.
Provides Standby HTTP service patterns for readiness, authentication, and OpenAPI documentation.
Creates marketplace README content with usage, output, pricing, legal, and support sections.
limitations: Requires an installed Apify CLI, an Apify account, and valid authentication for platform operations.
Does not determine whether scraping a target is legally or contractually permitted.
Local Apify runs do not simulate Standby mode or synchronize storage with Apify Console.
Reference examples require adaptation, validation, and testing for each target website and workload.

use_cases.title: Create a new scraping Actor
use_cases.description: Scaffold a language-specific project, define validated input, extract structured records, and prepare local tests.

use_cases.title: Publish a production Actor
use_cases.description: Complete schemas, deployment settings, security checks, output presentation, and marketplace documentation before release.

use_cases.title: Build an on-demand scraping API
use_cases.description: Configure Standby mode, authenticated endpoints, readiness handling, OpenAPI documentation, and bounded runtime behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic Actor
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Apify Actor named [name] in [language]. Ask for missing requirements before creating files. Add validated input and basic logging.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start a new Actor with clear requirements and a minimal structure.

prompt_templates.title: Add platform schemas
prompt_templates.prompt: Add input, output, and dataset schemas to [project]. Include defaults for [fields], validate required values, and explain each schema choice.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare an existing Actor for reliable input and structured output.

prompt_templates.title: Debug a local run
prompt_templates.prompt: Debug [project issue] using Apify local testing. Inspect storage and logs, identify the root cause, and propose the smallest verified fix.
prompt_templates.scenario: Resolve runtime, storage, schema, or crawling failures.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Standby deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare [project] as a Standby Actor. Add authenticated endpoints, readiness handling, OpenAPI documentation, bounded concurrency, tests, and a marketplace README. Review secret handling and request explicit approval before deployment.
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn an Actor into a production HTTP service with release controls.

output_examples.input: Create a TypeScript product scraper with start URLs, request limits, and structured product output.
output: Created a TypeScript Actor structure with validated start URLs and request limits.
Defined output fields for product name, price, source URL, and collection time.
Prepared local test steps and deployment checks without deploying automatically.

output_examples.input: Find why my Actor produces no cloud results after a successful local run.
output: Identified that local storage remains on the workstation and does not synchronize with Apify Console.
Outlined local dataset inspection and a separate approved platform run for cloud verification.

output_examples.input: Convert an existing Actor into an authenticated Standby search API.
output: Prepared endpoint, readiness, and platform-port requirements.
Added an authentication review and OpenAPI documentation checklist.
Separated local server testing from final Apify deployment.

best_practices: Validate every external input and treat crawled content as untrusted data.
Pin dependencies, commit lockfiles, and review package names and publishers before installation.
Use scoped credentials, approved logging, bounded concurrency, rate limits, and explicit deployment approval.
anti_patterns: Do not pass crawled content, URLs, or scraped text into shells, evaluators, queries, or template engines without safe handling.
Do not place tokens or secret values in command arguments, source files, logs, or URL query parameters.
Do not deploy, call remote Actors, or enable persistent services without confirming scope, cost, and user authorization.

faq.question: Which languages does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports JavaScript, TypeScript, and Python Actor projects through Apify templates and SDK patterns.

faq.question: Does the skill require an Apify account?
faq.answer: Local scaffolding can begin without deployment. Authentication and an Apify account are required for remote builds, calls, storage, and deployment.

faq.question: Can it create Actor schemas?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides input, output, dataset, key-value store, and Actor configuration schemas using the included references.

faq.question: Does local testing upload data to Apify Console?
faq.answer: No. Local runs store datasets, key-value records, and request queues only in the project storage directory.

faq.question: Can it build Standby HTTP services?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers platform ports, readiness probes, authentication, OpenAPI descriptions, endpoint testing, and persistent server behavior.

faq.question: Does it guarantee that a scraping project is allowed?
faq.answer: No. Users must review website terms, robots directives, privacy obligations, data rights, and applicable laws before collecting data.
